name: Benny Szabo
equipment: Keys to 'Wick Sightseer' double-decker tour bus #14 (diesel, three-quarters of a tank, open top deck, PA system, seats 64)
Wireless headset microphone and the belt-pack PA amplifier (battery 80%)
Clipboard tour manifest: 14 passengers on the 3:30 'Skyline & Harbor' loop
Tire iron from the bus's tool locker
A tour guide's umbrella with a yellow rubber duck taped to the tip, so people can follow it in a crowd
Two rolls of Mentos, a thermos of terrible coffee, and a laminated card of Merriwick facts he has not needed to read in twenty years
Phone (70% battery; he never uses it)
features: Human (Specialist) (+2 Charisma, +1 Constitution, one extra skill proficiency: Piloting)
Silver Tongue (expertise: double proficiency bonus on Persuasion and Insight)
Rally (bonus action: an ally who can hear him gains 1d6+3 temporary hit points and may end being frightened; 3 uses per long rest)
Union Card (Blue-Collar Worker feature: union workers — bus drivers, transit crews, sanitation, porters — will shelter him, help him and tell him what they have seen)
Class skills Persuasion, Insight and Performance; background skills Mechanics and Athletics; Specialist skill Piloting

personality.traits: I cannot not narrate. Put a microphone in my hand and I will tell you the history of the building that is on fire. I learn everyone's name in the first ten minutes and I use it, because a person whose name you know will follow you.
personality.ideals: You bring back as many as you took out. Fourteen got on the bus at 3:30. Fourteen get off.
personality.bonds: My fourteen: the Lindqvists from Malmö, the Okafors and their twins, the Brennan sisters from Cork, Mr. and Mrs. Tanaka, two backpackers from Leeds, a honeymoon couple from Ohio and a very old man called Mr. Feld who is travelling alone and has not said why.
personality.flaws: I am a performer. I need the crowd to love me and I will say the comforting thing instead of the true thing, every time, if I think it will keep them walking. And I talk — oh, how I talk — on an island where the quiet ones live.

appearance: A round, pink, cheerful Hungarian-American man of fifty-two with a magnificent grey moustache, a bald crown and the remains of a ponytail, in a yellow 'Wick Sightseer' windbreaker with a headset microphone permanently hooked over one ear. He walks with a slight roll from twenty years of standing on the top deck of a moving bus, and he holds a yellow umbrella with a rubber duck on it high over his head without seeming to notice he is doing it. When he smiles at you, you feel like the only tourist on the bus.
backstory: Benedek 'Benny' Szabo came to Merriwick at nineteen with a cousin's address and no English and has driven buses on the island for thirty-three years: eleven on the M-14 crosstown for the Transit Authority, then twenty-two for Wick Sightseer, where he discovered that he could make a busload of strangers from nine countries laugh at the same joke at the same time and has never got over it. He knows the story of every building on the 'Skyline & Harbor' loop and about a third of them are true. On the Thursday he has bus #14 at the kerb on Kestrel Avenue outside Union Terminal with fourteen passengers aboard, mid-way through his speech about the Terminal's ceiling, when the light changes, the PA fills with a tone that is not coming from his microphone, and a quarter of a mile down the cross street, over the rooftops, the whole river span of the Kingsgate Bridge rises into the air in one piece with the evening traffic still on it, and turns, and goes. His fourteen are looking at him. He keeps talking. He has no idea what he is saying, but he keeps talking, and they keep looking at him, and that turns out to be the most important thing anybody does in the first five minutes.
